title: JSON mode: soft-repair validator experiment and latency/safety trade-offs
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: evaluate a lightweight 'soft-repair' validator that repairs streamed JSON-mode outputs with minimal edits when constraint violations are detected, and compare it to (a) purely constrained decoding, and (b) post-hoc full-document repair. We need to quantify accuracy vs latency vs semantic drift for production streaming scenarios and design a safe canary rollout path.

Background: strict constrained-decoding ensures high schema adherence but increases token-level latency and often reduces output diversity. Full post-hoc repair improves adherence but can introduce large rewrites and surprising semantic changes. The soft-repair approach attempts token-local minimal fixes on the fly (e.g., balancing braces, closing arrays, minimal key-normalization) so the client can receive a stream that is valid-json incrementally, with a repair score attached.

Scope: engineering spike + baseline harness + canary config for Console canary traffic. Deliverables: experiment harness artifacts, perf/regression dashboards, draft canary policy, and a recommended rollout plan with guardrails for semantic-change threshold and user-visible indicators.
acceptance_criteria: Define and implement a soft-repair component that can run in the streaming pipeline and emit repaired tokens plus a repair_score header
Run A/B experiments comparing (constrained-decoding, soft-repair, post-hoc repair) across representative workloads and publish results to runtime-1.22 dashboard
Establish a semantic-drift metric (cosine sim on embeddings + token-diff heuristic) and set a safe threshold for canary fallback
Provide a canary rollout plan: % traffic split, abort conditions (schema-adherence < 99%, repair_rate > 2%, semantic-drift > threshold), and observability hooks
updates: 2026-02-10: Initial ticket created by Ava. Spike to compare approaches proposed. Linked to structured-output-stability project.

2026-02-15: Spike implemented: simple greedy repair that closes unmatched braces and trims trailing commas. Quick experiment on synthetic corpus shows adherence increase from 87% -> 96% with median added latency +6ms per token. Draft PR opened.

2026-02-18: Engineering review (S. Patel): suggested adding repair_score and attaching repair annotations to stream events instead of mutating original tokens where possible. Also requested tests for toolcall interference scenarios.

2026-02-22: Second iteration: soft-repair emits repair events (repair_start, repair_patch, repair_end) and includes a repair_score 0..1. Observability telemetry prototyped: repair_rate, avg_repair_size, repair_score_histogram.

2026-02-28: Perf regression observed on long-sequence streaming sessions (10k tokens): tail latency p99 increased by 18% in emulated constrained model. Investigating micro-optimizations and opportunistic batching for repair operations.
2026-03-03: PM review (Nina Thompson): requested semantic-drift evaluation and customer-impact assessment. Added in-production sample set from Console logs (anonymized).

2026-03-07: Experimental results: full constrained-decoding adherence 99.3% but avg token latency +22ms; post-hoc repair adherence 99.8% but semantic-drift (measured by embedding sim drop) = 0.12 on avg; soft-repair adherence 98.9% with avg latency +8ms and semantic-drift 0.03. Preliminary recommendation: soft-repair as default for streaming low-latency tier, constrained-decoding for strict-high-fidelity tier.

2026-03-10: Design feedback (Miguel Alvarez): add UX flag in Console for 'show repair annotations' for debugging canary users. Design provided mockups link. Preparing canary PR and canary dashboard widgets.
experiment_plan: Corpus: 6k prompts combining synthetic schema edgecases + 1k anonymized production samples
Variants: baseline (no repair), constrained-decoding (beam lexicon gating), soft-repair streaming, post-hoc repair
Metrics: schema_adherence_pct, avg_token_latency_ms, p95_stream_latency_ms, repair_rate_pct, median_repair_size_tokens, semantic_drift_score
Bench: run across model family variants (redwood/opt-13b, open/gpt-7b) and two hardware classes (A100, T4) to capture kernel-level performance effects
decisions: Keep soft-repair as a separate pluggable stage in the streaming pipeline (not baked into core constrained-decoder). Reason: allows per-tenant policy and simpler canary toggles.
Expose repair_score and repair annotations in stream events; do not mutate original token payload unless repair_score > 0.9 and repair is unambiguous.
Use combined metric (schema_adherence_pct weighted with semantic_drift_score) to decide canary abort rather than adherence alone.
Rollout plan: start at 1% traffic for non-enterprise customers with opt-in Console debugging UI, increase to 10% if metrics stable for 48h, then evaluate for tenant-level opt-ins.
